chat_history.content:
The World Health Organization (WHO) does not have specific guidelines for the recommended daily intake of vitamin D. However, other health organizations provide recommendations that are widely accepted. According to the National Institutes of Health (NIH), the recommended daily intake levels for vitamin D are as follows:

- Infants (0-12 months): 400 IU (10 mcg)
- Children (1-18 years): 600 IU (15 mcg)
- Adults (19-70 years): 600 IU (15 mcg)
- Adults (71 years and older): 800 IU (20 mcg)
- Pregnant and breastfeeding women: 600 IU (15 mcg)

For more detailed information, you can refer to the [NIH Vitamin D Fact Sheet](https://ods.od.nih.gov/factsheets/VitaminD-HealthProfessional/).
